name: Categorical Encoders Benchmark
description: Categorical encoders transform categorical features into numerical representations that are indispensable for a wide range of machine learning models. Existing encoder benchmark studies lack generalizability because of their limited choice of (1) encoders, (2) experimental factors, and (3) datasets. Additionally, inconsistencies arise from the adoption of varying aggregation strategies. This paper is the most comprehensive benchmark of categorical encoders to date, including an extensive evaluation of 32 configurations of encoders from diverse families, with 36 combinations of experimental factors, and on 50 datasets. The study shows the profound influence of dataset selection, experimental factors, and aggregation strategies on the benchmark's conclusions -- aspects disregarded in previous encoder benchmarks.
evaluation_method: predictive performance (classification: accuracy / AUC; regression: RMSE)
general_score_metric: predictive performance (accuracy for classification, RMSE for regression)
reputation: Comprehensive, recent benchmark for categorical encoders that is gaining attention among practitioners and researchers working on tabular-feature engineering.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focused on tabular data; results are highly sensitive to dataset selection, aggregation strategy, and downstream model choice; wide dataset heterogeneity (50 datasets) can make cross-dataset aggregation and ranking unstable.
